dedupe_keys.name: incontrol total airport management digital twin enterprise dynamics and pedestrian dynamics

description: InControl, a Dutch simulation software company, offers a Total Airport Management digital twin built on its Enterprise Dynamics discrete-event simulator and its Pedestrian Dynamics agent-based crowd simulator. The product page describes digital twins, including a predictive twin, as the basis of an airport operations centre that integrates passenger, baggage and cargo processes and those of airlines and other stakeholders. InControl states long experience in simulating baggage handling systems, passenger flows, cargo and border control and multimodal hubs, as well as train and cruise terminals. Examples on the page include queues at check-in and security, staff planning, timely evacuation of terminals and piers, and the redesign of the Multimodal Hub Schiphol, where Pedestrian Dynamics simulates a new public transport hub that handles about 109,000 travellers a day, expected to rise to about 120,000, with 140 buses an hour. Coverage: any airport or hub a customer models. Access: licensed software with trials and free student versions; models are project-specific. Licence and cost: proprietary and paid. Caveats: marketing material with no published validation, and models and data stay with customers. It supports digital twin, capacity planning, agent-based crowd and emergency evacuation studies of airports and transit hubs. It is a commercial counterpart to the open pedestrian simulators JuPedSim and Vadere and relates to the Jülich pedestrian dynamics data archive in the catalogue.
